clue.text: Still lacking action in Westminster?

parts.note: in Parliament at Westminster a proposal put to the House for debate is a motion
lacking means without, the suffix -less

explanation.surface: A jibe that Parliament never gets anything done.
explanation.definitionFit: Still describes something not moving at all, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Mean mix-up one's ushered in for United

indicators.note: ushered in for says one letter is brought in to take another's place

parts.note: a mix-up is a muddle
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An unkind confusion as someone is shown in to replace a United player.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the average, the middle value.

clue.text: In ramshackle motorboat Rob carelessly spilt fruit

indicators.note: ramshackle, rickety and disordered, signals the letters of motorboat are rearranged
carelessly spilt says the letters of Rob tumble out of the jumble, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: Rob drops his fruit overboard in a rickety boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange MOTORBOAT, and the letters of ROB fall out, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a tomato is a fruit, the seed-bearing part of the plant.

clue.text: Cosy in a local? Can be, sometimes

indicators.note: Can be hints the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pub is snug: it is now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean now and then, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: This year's long, especially affecting Pisceans for starters

indicators.note: for starters says take the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: This year is long, which affects people born under Pisces most of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle ran in a leap year (2016), and 29 February falls in the Pisces star sign, so the surface fits the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A year with an added 29 February is described with this adjective, as the puzzle's year was.

clue.text: Orderly dispatched round Channel Islands, provided freeze decreased

indicators.note: round says one piece goes around another

parts.note: dispatched means sent
CI abbreviates the Channel Islands, Jersey and Guernsey
provided as a conjunction means if

indicators.note: decreased means made smaller, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ice is frozen water, a freeze

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly posted around the Channel Islands, provided the cold weather eased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orderly' looks like a hospital worker but is the adjective, methodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientific approach is systematic and methodical.

clue.text: Some very ardent characters in court

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some characters in a courtroom are very passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtyard is an enclosed space, so its 'characters' are letters forming another word for a court.

clue.text: Summon up some breath lustily before energetic …

indicators.note: before places the hidden piece ahead of the next one
some says only part of the words is taken, the letters straddling the gap between them

parts.note: the words breath lustily written together, of which only a run across the word break is kept

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to summon someone to court is to cite them

explanation.surface: Puff and pant heartily before a vigorous effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' keeps ATHL, the letters spanning 'breath lustily', and 'up' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: An athletic person is strong, fit and vigorous.

clue.text: … smoothing of plaster?

definitions.meaning: ... stone or timber is smoothing and finishing its surface
a sticking plaster is a wound covering

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a vigorous smoothing of plaster on a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both finishing a surface smooth and a bandage put on a cut.

clue.text: March — and arctic winds, showing no favours

parts.note: a protest march is a demo

indicators.note: winds as a verb, twisting about, signals the letters of arctic are rearranged

explanation.surface: A picture of a March day with icy winds that spare nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' turns ARCTIC into CRATIC. 'March' looks like the month but is a protest walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A democratic system treats everyone equally, giving favour to nobody.

clue.text: Hedge fund finally scrapped dodgy spread

indicators.note: dodgy, unreliable or shifty, signals the remaining letters are jumbled
scrapped means thrown out, so a letter is removed
finally picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A financial tale: a hedge fund is shut down for being shady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes D from fund; 'scrapped' removes it from HEDGE, leaving HEGE, which 'dodgy' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used in Indian cooking, an example of something spread or used like butter.

clue.text: Creator of 'Top Team' actuality more confident after sacking lead

indicators.note: after places the trimmed word at the end

parts.note: Man U, Manchester United, is a top English football team
an actuality is a fact

indicators.note: sacking lead means dismissing the first letter

parts.note: more confident is surer

explanation.surface: A tabloid line about whoever made the 'Top Team' programme getting cocky after firing the star.
explanation.definitionFit: A manufacturer makes goods, the maker or producer of them.

clue.text: Note: exam's up-to-date

parts.note: la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A memo announcing that the exam is current.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent version of something is the newest, fully current one.

clue.text: Assailants wearing boots, as Klaus might say

parts.note: wearing clothes is being in them, IN

indicators.note: Klaus is a stock German name, and a German accent turns an English W into a V sound

parts.note: waders are thigh-high waterproof boots worn by anglers

explanation.surface: Attackers stomping in heavy boots, described in a German accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Waders are thigh-high waterproof boots worn by anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaders are attackers who enter territory by force.

clue.text: In particular, showing sixth sense, Cecil's 'stuffing' supporter

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the sixth sense

indicators.note: the stuffing of a word is its insides, all but the ends

parts.note: a supporter is an ally

explanation.surface: Cecil shows uncanny insight into stuffing a turkey, aided by a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases single something out above the rest, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Tory's bird out in dreadful make-up

parts.note: a Tory is a Conservative, CON, plus the S of the possessive
the tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: dreadful, terribly done, signals the letters of out in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Conservative's girlfriend is out in hideous cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's make-up is their physical or mental constitution, their basic nature.

clue.text: Dear me — HM's badly clobbered …

indicators.note: badly, done poorly, signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An exclamation of dismay that Her Majesty has been beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her Majesty; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammered and clobbered both mean beaten heavily, or soundly defeated.

clue.text: … in the head; USA trips unlikely

indicators.note: unlikely, improbable, signals the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: struck on the head, so trips to the US are improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, what goes on upstairs is what happens in the mind or brain.

clue.text: Paella batch I stupidly ordered by letter

indicators.note: stupidly, done without sense, signals the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook confesses to messing up the paella order.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged in A-to-Z sequence by initial characters, as in a dictionary.

clue.text: Settle bill with fair

parts.note: a bill, a poster, is an ad
fair means just

explanation.surface: Pay the invoice equitably.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle something into place is to correct or set it right.

clue.text: Lowland over the hill held by emperor's central detachment

indicators.note: held by says one piece sits inside another
central detachment means the centre of the word is detached and kept

parts.note: someone over the hill is old

explanation.surface: A low area over the hill held by a detachment of the emperor's troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A polder is low land reclaimed from the sea, as in the Netherlands.

clue.text: Setter receiving great kick in the guts — from copper?

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as ME, here taking on what follows
great in the sense of big, tall

indicators.note: the guts of a word are its middle letters

explanation.surface: The setter suffers a heavy blow to the stomach, perhaps from a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but the definition reads it as the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of or resembling copper is of a metal, the adjective form.

clue.text: Workroom outside's unfinished and deteriorating

indicators.note: deteriorating, falling apart, signals the letters are rearranged
unfinished means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: the word outside used as written

explanation.surface: A shabby workshop whose exterior has never been completed and is decaying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops E to give OUTSID, which 'deteriorating' rearranges; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or photographer's working room.

clue.text: Perjurer's report's one with strings attached

indicators.note: a report is a sound, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a perjurer lies under oath, a liar

explanation.surface: A perjurer's testimony comes with conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is a harp-like instrument, and an instrument with strings is cryptically something with strings attached.

clue.text: Arcadians regularly getting wet

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Inhabitants of idyllic Arcadia keep getting soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: The wet is a noun for rainy weather, as in 'out in the wet'.

clue.text: Holiday region has infestation mentioned on every side

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: an infestation of pests is a plague
on every side means round, surrounding

explanation.surface: A holiday area that is besieged by vermin all around.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground is a place for fun and recreation, and a resort can be called a holidaymakers' playground.

clue.text: Ashes of French saint

parts.note: du is French for 'of the'

explanation.surface: The cremated remains of a French saint, relics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashes and dust are both the powdery remains of something burnt or decayed.

clue.text: Printer using extremes of technology with metal to impress Royal Institution

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
to impress means to press into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: pewter is a tin alloy, a metal
RI abbreviates the Royal Institution, the London science body

explanation.surface: A tech printer built with metal to wow a scientific society.
explanation.definitionFit: A typewriter prints characters on paper key by key, a printing machine.
